source.title: Specialized coding of sensory, motor and cognitive variables in VTA dopamine neurons

confidence_rationale: This is the direct measurement the crux question calls for: two-photon imaging of >300 individual VTA dopamine neurons during a complex virtual-reality decision task, resolving population structure rather than assuming it. The finding is genuinely mixed with respect to MECH-069's strong reading. Against a pure uniform-scalar-RPE null, the paper finds functional specialization -- subpopulations of dopamine neurons preferentially transmit sensory, motor, or cognitive/choice-related variables, and these functional clusters are spatially organized and aligned with projection topography, which is exactly the kind of anatomically-grounded channel separation MECH-069 needs. Against MECH-069's specific three-way partition, the paper's own framing is multiplexing, not a clean E1/E2/E3-shaped trichotomy: most individual neurons carry mixtures of variables rather than one pure error type, and the recorded variables (position, velocity, choice, reward, cue identity) don't map one-to-one onto REE's E1 (sensory prediction)/E2 (motor-sensory on z_gamma)/E3 (harm/goal) partition -- there is no dedicated 'harm' variable in this reward-only task at all, so the paper cannot speak to E3's separateness. Confidence is moderate: strong source quality and a genuine measurement of the crux (heterogeneity vs. uniform broadcast), but mapping fidelity to the SPECIFIC three-way epistemic-type cut is only partial.
failure_signatures: Individual dopamine neurons in this dataset are frequently mixed-selectivity (multiplexing several variables), not cleanly single-channel -- a strong single-error-type reading of MECH-069 (one neuron, one error type) is not what was measured; the paper's unit of separation is functional CLUSTERS of neurons, not single-neuron purity.

The task has no genuine harm/punishment dimension (it is a reward-seeking VR navigation task), so this paper offers no direct evidence for or against E3 (harm/goal error) being a distinct channel from E1/E2 -- it only speaks to the E1-vs-E2-vs-cognitive-variable side of the partition.

mapping.source_claim_statement: VTA dopamine neurons are not a homogeneous population emitting one scalar reward-prediction-error signal; they show functionally specialized, spatially clustered, anatomically-topographic coding of distinct sensory, motor and cognitive variables in addition to reward.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-069 asserts REE's three error channels (E1 sensory-prediction, E2 motor-sensory, E3 harm/goal) are incommensurable and must remain structurally separate. Engelhard et al. supply the general form of evidence MECH-069 needs -- a demonstrated departure from the classical single-scalar-RPE dopamine model toward genuine, anatomically-organized functional specialization -- without supplying the specific three-way epistemic-type partition. It is evidence that SOME structured channel separation exists in the brain's actual reward/prediction-error machinery, which is the necessary precondition for MECH-069's stronger claim, but not itself confirmation of the E1/E2/E3 split specifically.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's 'specialization' is at the level of neuronal subpopulations carrying weighted combinations of task variables, not a clean partition into non-overlapping error TYPES; and the task offers no harm/aversive dimension, so E3 is untested here. Treat this as supporting the general plausibility of heterogeneous, structured DA coding -- not as direct confirmation of REE's specific trichotomy.
mapping.source_context: Mouse, head-fixed virtual-reality accumulation-of-evidence navigation task; two-photon calcium imaging of VTA dopamine neurons; reward-only paradigm (no punishment/harm condition).

confidence_components.notes: Landmark, high-N single-unit imaging study in a top venue; the crux measurement (heterogeneity vs. uniform broadcast) is exactly on point. Mapping fidelity is capped in the middle because the paper's functional clusters are multiplexed rather than a clean three-way epistemic-type split, and the task cannot speak to the E3/harm arm of MECH-069 at all.
